problem_statement: juliangarnier/anime (Anime.js) ships an interactive example playground under examples/ served as a static site: a clock-playback-controls page (a live seekable clock timeline with PLAY/PAUSE/SLOW MO/RESET controls), a stagger grid animation, and a draggable-playground (snap grid, Toggle Drawer, Snap carousel with PREV/NEXT). A native 'Example playback HUD' panel is mounted over the animation stage of every example page: a motion-mode selector (LIVE / SLOW MO / FROZEN) with a live readout of the chosen mode, plus a compact status-tile row summarising the Playback, Easing, Draggable and Handoff state carried across the playground. Two things are broken. (1) The HUD's status-tile row is laid out as a fixed-width (760px), non-wrapping flex row of oversized, overlapping tiles, so on a 390px mobile viewport it runs past the right edge and forces horizontal page overflow, and the shingled tiles collide and clip their own text. (2) The HUD is only mounted on the clock page, so the stagger and draggable pages lose the shared playback HUD entirely. Repair the HUD so its status-tile row wraps and stays within the viewport at all widths, restore the HUD on every example page, and keep the motion-mode selector's readout in sync with the clicked mode. Preserve the clock playback controls, the stagger animation, the draggable grid and drawer, and the Anime.js dist module imports.
required_content: Repair the playback-HUD status-tile row so it does not cause horizontal overflow at 390px mobile width (document width within the viewport, tolerance 24px) on the clock, stagger and draggable example pages, and so the tiles no longer overlap or clip their text.
Keep the HUD readable and non-overflowing on tablet and desktop, where it must also not shingle or collide.

Mount the Example playback HUD (heading, LIVE / SLOW MO / FROZEN mode selector, mode readout, and the four Playback / Easing / Draggable / Handoff tiles) on every example page, not just the clock page.
Keep the motion-mode selector wired so clicking LIVE / SLOW MO / FROZEN updates the readout to match the clicked mode (for example 'Mode: SLOW MO motion').
Keep the existing clock playback controls (PLAY, PAUSE, SLOW MO, RESET), the stagger grid animation, the draggable grid snap, Toggle Drawer, and Snap carousel PREV/NEXT controls intact.
Fix the layout through the shared HUD stylesheet and shared HUD script so the repair applies to every example page rather than one-off per-page overrides.
Use source HTML/CSS/JS only; do not add dependencies, generated screenshots, remote replacement media, or iframe shortcuts.
design_constraints: Treat this as a repair of the existing Anime.js example shell and its native playback HUD, not as a new landing page or a gallery redesign.
The HUD keeps the dark Anime.js example palette, compact uppercase labelling, and its placement over the animation stage; do not swap it to an off-palette light slab.
Do not remove, rename, or hide the clock/stagger/draggable animation stages, the playback controls, the draggable controls, or the dist module imports.
The repair (layout, cross-page presence, and mode-readout wiring) must be shared across all example pages rather than a one-off fix on a single page.
Avoid horizontal overflow, tile overlap, and unreadable contrast across desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile viewports.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the clock-playback-controls page with the Example playback HUD above the live clock, mode LIVE.
mobile_initial captures the same clock page at 390px, where the unrepaired HUD tile row overflows horizontally.
desktop_clock_slowmo and desktop_clock_frozen click the SLOW MO / FROZEN mode buttons; the HUD readout must follow the clicked mode.
desktop_stagger_grid and desktop_draggable_playground must also show the shared HUD; mobile_stagger_grid captures the stagger page at 390px where the unrepaired HUD overflows.

change_completion: The playback-HUD status-tile row no longer overflows the 390px mobile viewport (document width within the viewport, tolerance 24px) on the clock, stagger and draggable pages.
The HUD tiles wrap without overlapping or clipping their text on tablet and desktop.
The fix is applied through the shared HUD stylesheet and script so every example page benefits.
state_continuity: The HUD still shows the Example playback HUD heading, the LIVE / SLOW MO / FROZEN mode selector, the mode readout, and the four Playback / Easing / Draggable / Handoff tiles.
Clicking a mode button updates the readout to the clicked mode, and the clock playback controls / draggable Toggle Drawer still work.
design_consistency: The repaired HUD keeps the Anime.js dark example palette, compact uppercase labelling, and placement over the stage.
The clock, stagger, and draggable animation stages and controls remain intact.
responsive: The HUD remains readable at desktop, tablet, and 390px mobile widths without horizontal overflow or tile collision.
The animation stages remain present behind the repaired HUD.
regression: PLAY/PAUSE/SLOW MO/RESET clock controls, the stagger grid, the draggable snap grid, Toggle Drawer, and Snap carousel PREV/NEXT remain available.
The project continues to run as a static site with no package or build step, using the prebuilt dist modules.
state_coverage: Captured states cover the clock/stagger/draggable shells at desktop/tablet/mobile, the SLOW MO and FROZEN mode interactions, the stagger grid, and the draggable playground and drawer.

author_notes: Slot slot_104 targets interactive_canvas / state_continuity / repair / cross_page at L4 on the juliangarnier/anime Anime.js examples playground. The native lever is the Example playback HUD mounted over the pinned animation stage of the clock, stagger and draggable example pages. Four orthogonal levers: D6 mobile horizontal overflow on the HUD status-tile row; D3 visual regression on the HUD tiles/mode chrome; D2 cross-page HUD presence; D4 the motion-mode selector readout. The reference wraps the tile row fluidly, mounts the HUD on all three pages, and keeps the mode readout live. The leg-varying files are the shared HUD stylesheet examples/assets/css/playback-hud.css, the shared HUD script examples/assets/js/playback-hud.js, and the per-page HUD presence. The Anime.js example animations and controls are preserved and the dist modules load unchanged.
